 JUDGMENT
This petition under Section 166 Motor Vehicles Act, 1989 is filed seeking compensation of .30,00,000/- for the death of Prashant Kumar B. S/o Babu in a road traffic accident.

2. It is stated in the petition that on 21-03-2023 about 11.30 p.m. Prashant Kumar was proceeding as a pillion rider in a motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-KL- 2343 (herein after called as offending vehicle) and his friend was the rider and when they reached near Kote Junction, BB Road,
Devanahalli, Bengaluru, the rider of said motorcycle rode the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, lost control on the vehicle, due to which he jumped the motorcycle on the road hump and dashed to a Car bearing No.KA-36-N-6683.
Due to the accident, they fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately he was taken to Shirdi Sai hospital, but on the way he succumbed to the injuries.
After, postmortem the Petitioners have received the dead body and performed his last rites.
3. It is stated that Petitioner No.1 is the mother and Petitioner No.2 and 3 are the elder brothers of the deceased.
Prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy, aged about 22 years and he was working in a Shamiyana house and earning .30,000/- p.m.

The Petitioner No.1 to 3 being the mother and brothers of deceased and they were depending upon the income of deceased and due to untimely death of deceased, they have suffered mental shock and agony and lost their bread earner of the family.
The Petitioners have spent huge amount towards transportation and funeral and obsequious ceremonies.
The Petitioners have stated that the rider of the offending vehicle is solely responsible for the cause of the said accident.

Hence, it is requested to award .30,00,000/-
compensation with interest from the Respondent No.1 and 2 being the insurer and insured of the alleged vehicle.
4. In response to the petition notice, Respondent No.1 has appeared before the court through its counsel and filed the objections.
The respondent No.2 has not appeared before the court and she was placed exparte.
5. The Respondent No.1-in its objection statement has admitted the issuance of policy.
However, its liability is subject to terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.

It has It has contended that the owner of the offending vehicle and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory Maria vs Liberty General Insurance Co. Ltd on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140273407/
2 provisions of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.

It has contended that the accident has occurred due to sole negligence of deceased himself as he was riding the motorbike and rider was not covered under the policy as such, petition is not maintainable for one's own negligence.
It has contended that the rider of offending vehicle was not having valid DL.
It has contended that the compensation claimed is highly excessive.

It has denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased,
relationship of Petitioners with the deceased and their dependency and prayed for dismissal of the petition.
6. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues have been framed :-

1 . Whether the petitioners prove that death of Prashant Kumar B. S/o.Babu, was only due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA- 04-KL-2343 on 21-03-2023 at about 8- 11.30 p.m., on BB Road, near Kote Junction Devanahalli, Bengaluru Rural District?
2. What compensation petitioners are entitled?
3. What order ?

7. In support of their claim, 2nd Petitioner is examined as PW.1 and got marked the documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.12.
8.

The Respondent No.1-Insurance company has examined its official as RW-1 and got marked the copy of policy at Ex.R.1.
9.
I heard the counsel on both sides and have perused the material on record.

Learned counsel for respondent No.1 has filed a citation reported in Special Leave Petition (civil) No.1110/2017 SCC.
10.

By considering the evidence and materials available on record and after hearing the arguments my findings to the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 11. ISSUE NO.1:- PW-1 has stated that onon 21-03-2023 about 11.30 p.m. Prashant Kumar was proceeding as a pillion rider in the offending vehicle and his friend was the rider and when they reached near Kote Junction, BB Road, Devanahalli, Bengaluru, the rider of said motorcycle rode the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, lost control on the vehicle, due to which he jumped the motorcycle on the road hump and dashed to a Car bearing No.KA-36-N-6683.
Due to the accident, they fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately he was taken to Shirdi Sai hospital, but on the way he succumbed to the fatal injuries.
The accident was due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Maria vs Liberty General Insurance Co. Ltd on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140273407/
3

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
12. PW-1 has relied on the police documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P.8 i.e. FIR, complaint, spot mahazar,
spot sketch, IMV report, inquest report, PM report and charge sheet.
Petitioners have relied on the police records, according to police records it was the negligence of the rider of the motor cycle.

13. Respondent No.1-insurance company has contended that deceased himself rode the motorcycle in high speed and negligently dashed to the car as he had no DL, by knowing the fact that the compensation would not be granted and thereby it was falsely stated that deceased's friend was riding the motorcycle.

The petitioners in active collusion with the police have falsely implicated the offending motorcycle by alleging that the deceased was proceeding in the offending vehicle as a pillion rider and one of his friend Mahesh who rode his vehicle in a rash and negligent manner in a high speed and lost the control of his vehicle and dashed against the car which was going in the same way.
During the course of cross-examination of PW1 the same suggestion has been put forth by the learned counsel for the Respondent no 1.
PW-1 has denied this suggestion.

Except these suggestions, there are no documents to show that deceased was riding the motorcycle in high speed and negligently dashed to the car as he has had no DL, by knowing the fact that the compensation would not be granted and thereby it was falsely stated that deceased's friend Mahesh was riding the motorcycle.

The learned counsel for the Respondent no 1 has relied upon the decision rendered in Special leave petition (civil) no 1110/2017 between Safiq Ahmad Vs ICICI Lombard General Insurance Co Ltd & Others.

entities.text: Safiq Ahmad Vs ICICI Lombard General Insurance Co Ltd & Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that the modus operandi in instituting the fake compensation petitions.

Some of the modus Operandi adopted are as under non-road accident injury-death converted into road accident claims; fraudulent implantation of vehicle, false implantation of driver,claimant implantation,fake/ fabricated insurance polices,
fake/fabricated income documents/medical documents for exaggerated compensation.
14.
Keeping in view of the arguments and in view of the view of above decision, once again I have perused material available on record,
Complaint is given immediately after the accident by the driver/owner of the car bearing no KA-36-N-6683.
After investigation, it has been found that it was the negligence of rider of the offending vehicle.
The charge sheet is filed against the rider of the offending vehicle.
Absolutely there are no materials to overcome the charge sheet findings.

Though the official of the Respondent no 1 examined as RW1, Respondent no.1 has not placed any materials to disprove the negligence rode of the rider of the offending vehicle and there is no proper explanation on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle or driver of the car bearing no KA-36-N-6683 by examining them with regard to the manner in which the accident had occurred.
Therefore, the contention raised by the Respondent no 1 holds no water.

Petitioners have proved that it was the negligence of rider of the motor cycle who rode it in rash and negligent manner and dashed the motorcycle, due to which Prashanth Kumar died of severe injuries.
Hence, this Issue is answered in the Affirmative.
15. ISSUE NO.2:- Petitioner no 1 is the mother and brother of the deceased.
In order to prove their relationship, PW-1 has produced the inquest report and Aadhaar cards of the Petitioners, they are marked at Ex.P.10 to12.

The details in the above record show that deceased Prashanth Kumar is the son of Petitioner No.1 and the Petitioner No.2 and 3 are the brothers of the deceased. PW-1 - brother of the deceased has stated that he is doing car service work and his brother is doing coolie.

The petitioner no 2 and 3 have independent income and were not dependent on the income of the Maria vs Liberty General Insurance Co. Ltd on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140273407/
4 deceased and thereby they are not considered as dependent of the deceased.

entities.text: Maria vs Liberty General Insurance Co. Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Only Petitioner no 1 is considered as dependent upon the income of the deceased.

16. On perusal of records, it is found that Petitioners have produced the Aadhar card of deceased at Ex.P.9, which shows the date of birth as 27/04/2001 and as such, age of the deceased is considered as 22 years at the time of accident and appropriate multiplier applicable is 18.
17.
It is stated that deceased Prashanth Kumar was working in shamiyana house and was getting salary of Rs 30,000- P.M.
due to accident and untimely death of the deceased all the petitioners are put to great financial loss and mental agony .

To prove the income and avocation of the deceased,
the Petitioners have not produced any documents.
In the absence of proof of income, by considering age of the deceased and date of accident, notional income of Rs.16,000/- per month is taken.
18. As the deceased was aged about 22 years, future prospects of 40% is added on the income of the deceased.
Then the income would be .22,400/-.
Since, deceased was bachelor, 50% of his income shall be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.
Then the income is .11,200/- The loss of dependency would be .11,200 x 12 x 18 =.24,19,200/-.
19. CONSORTIUM:

By following the guidelines of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs- Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram & Others1, this Tribunal deems it proper to hold that the Petitioners are entitled .40,000/- each under the head of filial consortium as the Petitioner 1 No.1 has lost her son, who was support for her and Petitioner No 2 and 3 have lost their brother.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs- Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram & Others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 20. Loss to estate:
The loss to the estate is the loss of savings by the deceased.
It appears that the Petitioner No.1 has lost her son and Petitioner No.2 and 3 have lost their brother.

Hence, .15,000/-
towards loss to estate.
21. Transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies Expenses:
Petitioners have not claimed any compensation towards transportation of dead body, funeral & obsequies ceremony expenses.
By considering the facts and circumstances, it would be proper to award .15,000/- for the transportation of dead body, funeral & other incidental expenses.

22. In all, the amount of compensation awarded by this Tribunal to the Petitioners under various headings is as follows :
 Nature of Compensation Amount  1. Loss of dependency . 24,19,200/-
 2. Loss of Consortium . 1,20,000/-
 3. Loss to estate . 15,000/-
 4. Transportation of dead body, . 15,000/-
Maria vs Liberty General Insurance Co. Ltd on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140273407/
5  Funeral & obsequies  Expenses  Total . 25,69,200/-
23. Liability:

entities.text: Maria vs Liberty General Insurance Co. Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is already held that the rider of offending vehicle was negligent in causing the accident.
Therefore, Respondent No.1 and 2 being insurer and insured are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
However, Respondent No.1 is liable to pay the above compensation to the Petitioners with interest at 6% p.a.
With these observations I answer Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.

24. ISSUE NO.3 : In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos. 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V. Act is allowed in part with cost.

Petitioners are awarded compensation of .25,69,200/- together with interest @ 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till the realization.
Respondent No.1 shall deposit the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of amount, a sum of Rs.50,000/- each is apportioned to Petitioner No.2 and 3 and remaining amount is apportioned to Petitioner No.1.

Out of the said apportioned amount, 25% shall be kept in FD in the name of Petitioner No.1 in any nationalized or scheduled bank of her choice for a period of 2 years and remaining 75% with entire interest shall be disbursed to her through E-payment on proper identification.
The entire apportioned amount with interest awarded to the Petitioner No.2 and 3 shall be disbursed to them through E- payment on proper identification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly over the computer, typed by her, signed and pronounced by me in open court dated this the 12th day of December 2024).
(SHYLA S.M.) II Addl. Judge, ACJM & Member, MACT Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru.
